Shri Sankalp Kochar - Advocate for the petitioner.

Shri Amit Kumar Chaturvedi- Advocate for respondent N  VC.
 Shri Yadvendra Dwivedi - PL for respondent/State.

ORDER By way of this writ petition, the petitioner is not challenging any particular order and seeking a direction through this court to direct the respondents authorities to register an FIR against the respondent No. 7 because he has tempered several admission register and students marksheets and also prepared the forged documents regarding admission of students in the Government Primary School Mangawan Sankul, Government Higher Secondary School, Gandhiwara Block Chhindwara.

entities.text: Government Higher Secondary School, Gandhiwara Block Chhindwara
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. The petitioner has preferred following reliefs as prayed in paragraph-7 of petition which are as follows:-
"(i) Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and direct respondent No. 1 to 5 to immediately register an FIR u/ss 420, 464,465,467,468 and 471 of IPC against the Respondent No. 7.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10273 2 WP-36970-2025 (ii) That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and direct the Respondents 5 and 6 to initiate departmental enquiry against Respondentno.7 for imposition of major penalty under the applicable service rules and suspend Respondent No.7 with immediate effect and take any other necessary disciplinary action and also impose a fine.

1 (iii) Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be issued along with cost of the petition."
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that various complaints and representations were made by the petitioner to higher authorities regarding embezzlement of public funds by respondent No. 7 and even after preliminary inquiry report which stated that the allegations made against the respondent No. 7 are found to be true, the Government authorities took no coercive action against the respondent No. 7 and no FIR was registered against him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted that the petitioner came to know that respondent No. 7 has given admission to some students twice or thrice in successive years and therefore, embezzled the funds of Education Guarantee Scheme deceitfully.
It is further submitted that respondent No. 7, who is posted as a teacher has forged the medical documents to avoid transfer from Mangaon Primary School.

The complaint/representation made by the petitioner has been verified by the department and the department conducted an inquiry in which prima facie constitute a criminal offence in spite of that no FIR was registered by the authorities and on disciplinary inquiry, minor penalty was imposed against the respondent No. 7.

As per the inquiry report, respondent No. 7 had forged the admission documents, date of birth of students, enrolled the same students twice with a different date of birth and unlawfully availed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10273 3 WP-36970-2025 the benefits from the department.
The respondent No. 7 has manipulated the admission process and has made false admission in the school and therefore, prayed for registration of FIR against the respondent No.7.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Vinod Kumar Pandey and Anr. vs. Sheesh Ram Saini & Ors.( SLP No. 7900/2019) 2025 INSC 1095.
6.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted that upon complaint respondent authorities constituted a Committee against respondent No. 7 and District Planning Co-ordinator, Zilla Shikshak Kendra, Chhindwara and Block Education Officer Parasia and BRC Janpad Shiksha Kendra Parasia have jointly inquired the case and submitted inquiry report before the respondent No. 5 and thereafter, respondent No. 5 considered the inquiry report and passed order dated 28-11-2024, in which, two increments has been withheld with non-cumulative effect against the respondent No. 7.
7.

It is further submitted that grievance of the petitioner is to register an FIR against respondent No.
7 although, the respondent No. 7 has already registered an FIR against the petitioner prior to this incident, and therefore, on the basis of that FIR, the petitioner has made many complaints against the respondent No. 7 as a counter-blast.
Since, the petitioner has remedy to file private complaint before the learned trial Court under Section 200 of Cr.P.C and Section 223 of BNSS, 2023.
Reliance has been placed on the judgment of Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Sudhir Bhaskar Rao Tambe vs. Hemant Yashwant Dhange and Ors.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the Respondent No. 7 has submitted that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:10273 4 WP-36970-2025 instant petition is gross abuse of process of law and filed with malicious and ulterior motive to harass and settle personal scores with respondent No. 7.
The petitioner being a third party has no locus standi to institute the present petition before this Court.

It is further submitted that the FIR has already been registered against the petitioner at the instance of respondent No.7 and therefore, the present petition is a counter-blast and desperate attempt for seeking revenge.
9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10. Perusal of the record reflects that upon inquiry report dated 28- 11-2024, a departmental inquiry was constituted by the competent authority, Education Department and the State Authorities and in the departmental inquiry, penalty was imposed to the respondent No. 7 withholding two annual increments.

It also appears that respondent No. 7 has registered an FIR against the petitioner dated 14-06-2023 under Sections 424, 467,468 and 471 of IPC at Police Station Kundipara District Chhindwara which is registered as Crime No. 426/23.
To take revenge, petitioner has filed numbers of complaints against the respondent No. 7
and when FIR has not been registered against the respondent No. 7, to wreck vengeance, this petition has been filed by the petitioner.
11. On perusal of documents and inquiry report, it is prima facie clear that the Government has not suffered any financial losses.

The inquiry report indicate/suggests that respondent No. 7, who is a teacher/Guruji in that school showed students has enrolled in the school to save his job, even though, those students were not actually studying in that school.
Whether NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10273 5 WP-36970-2025 few or many children attended the school, it does not place any financial gains to the teachers.

12. On the basis of inquiry conducted by the authorities, a departmental inquiry has been constituted against the respondent No. 7, by which, penalty was imposed against him withholding two annual increments in the departmental inquiry.

When these facts are taken into consideration and considering the nature of allegations, this court is of the opinion that this is not a fit case to exercise inherent power vested in this court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C against respondent No. 7.
13.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

(B. P. SHARMA) JUDGE PG Manoj Singh Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33886720/
